name: Nystatin
executiveSummary: Topical GI polyene (negligible absorption). Oral thrush adult: **400,000–600,000 IU PO q6h** (swish & swallow). Infants: **100,000–200,000 IU q6h**. Intestinal: **500,000–1,000,000 IU q8h**.
indications:
## Indications

- Oropharyngeal and non-invasive GI candidiasis.
- Prophylaxis in immunosuppression/prolonged antibiotics (local protocols).

## Precautions

- Not for systemic or severe esophageal candidiasis (use systemic azoles).
- Shake suspension; hold in mouth before swallowing.

> Usual suspension: **100,000 IU/mL**.

adulto.presentation: Suspension 100,000 IU/mL; tablets/ovules by brand (vaginal topical separate).
adulto.administration: Swish several minutes then swallow; after meals; avoid immediate drinking.
adulto.notes: Continue a few days after clinical improvement.

pediatrico.dose: Infants/children: **1–2 mL (100,000–200,000 IU) q6h** to each side of the mouth. Older: up to adult doses if needed.
pediatrico.administration: Apply with dropper/swab to mucosa; swallow remainder.
pediatrico.notes: Treat maternal nipples if breastfeeding with thrush.

neonatal.dose: Often **100,000 IU (1 mL) q6h** to oral mucosa — local protocol.
neonatal.notes: Exclude invasive disease if no improvement.

stability:
## Stability

- Store per label; shake before use.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Nausea, diarrhea, local irritation; rare allergy (minimal systemic absorption).

bibliography.citation: Hospital Garrahan. Formulary — topical oral antifungals.
